answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity to complete a Wesolowski VDF: a continuous chain of modular squarings in which every next state depends on the preceding one. An attacker can copy labels, but simulating multiple clones cannot parallelize any chain across GPUs; each clone incurs its own sequential delay and computation. Thus wall-clock time, rather than cheap key generation, limits identities named orchard, ember, or opal.
